title: AI-Driven RF-Based Object Detection and Classification for 5G-Advanced and Beyond
summary: HFCL proposes AI-based radio-frequency sensing for telecom, transport, manufacturing, and monitoring applications, without a reported testbed outcome.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The concept uses radio signals to detect and classify objects, including where optical sensors are limited. Proposed applications include traffic, maintenance, infrastructure monitoring, and security. The source gives no testbed result or measured deployment benefit.
purpose: Use radio-frequency sensing to support detection and monitoring tasks.
system: AI-Driven RF-Based Object Detection and Classification for 5G-Advanced and Beyond

ratings.reason: RF sensing applications are described with no testbed or observed network/manufacturing result.
Public safety, digital inclusion, and emissions benefits are proposed.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 10: AI-Driven RF-Based Object Detection and Classification for 5G-Advanced and Beyond

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: AI radio sensing proposes new network and monitoring functions
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
